questions.question: Which classical dance originated in the South Indian state of Tamil Nadu and is traditionally performed as a devotional offering in temples?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is a pre-eminent Indian classical dance form that originated in the **Tanjore district** of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• Historically known as **Sadir** or **Dasi Attam**, it was performed as a **devotional offering** by **Devadasis** in Hindu temples.
 
• The dance is deeply rooted in the **Natya Shastra**, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts written by the sage **Bharata Muni** between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
 
• It is distinguished by its **geometric movements**, the **Araimandi** (half-sitting) posture, and intricate **Mudras** (hand gestures) used for storytelling.
 
• The performance repertoire typically includes **Alarippu**, **Jatiswaram**, **Shabdam**, **Varnam**, **Padam**, and **Tillana**, accompanied by **Carnatic music**.
 
• The revival of this dance form in the 20th century is largely credited to **E. Krishna Iyer** and **Rukmini Devi Arundale**, who founded **Kalakshetra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**:

 
 
• Originates from **North India**, particularly **Uttar Pradesh**, and is derived from the word **Katha** meaning storyteller.
 
• Features heavy **footwork** (Tatkar), lightning-fast **pirouettes** (Chakkars), and influences from both **Hindu** and **Mughal** cultures.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**:
 
 
• Hails from the state of **Odisha** and is characterized by the **Tribhanga** posture, where the body is bent at the neck, torso, and knees.
 
• It was historically performed by **Maharis** in temples and **Gotipuas** in public spaces.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**:
 
 
• A classical dance form from **Kerala**, known as the **Dance of the Enchantress** (Mohini).
 
• It is traditionally a solo female dance characterized by **graceful, swaying movements** that mimic the palm trees of Kerala.

questions.question: What is the focus of the 6G research project at IIIT-Naya Raipur under the TTDF scheme of DST?

options.text: Building an AI-driven telecom cloud platform.
Developing a prototype for 6G cell-free communication.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Developing a prototype for 6G cell-free communication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The research project at **IIIT-Naya Raipur** (Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee International Institute of Information Technology) focuses on building a functional prototype for **6G cell-free massive MIMO** (Multiple Input Multiple Output) technology.
 
• This initiative is funded under the **Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF)**, which is a specialized scheme by the **Department of Telecommunications (DoT)** (often associated with the broader research goals of **DST** in multi-departmental collaborations) to foster indigenous telecom innovations.
 
• **Cell-free communication** is a paradigm shift from traditional **cellular architectures** (like 4G and 5G) where users are served by specific base stations; instead, it uses a distributed network of **Access Points (APs)** to serve users cooperatively.
 
• The primary objective of this prototype is to eliminate the **cell-edge problem**, ensuring that users experience uniform, high-speed connectivity regardless of their physical location within the network coverage.
 
• The project aligns with the **Bharat 6G Vision**, which aims to position **India** as a global contributor to **6G standards** and technology deployment by the year **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Technology Development Fund (TTDF):**

 
 
• Launched to provide financial support to **domestic companies**, **startups**, and **academic institutions** for R&D in the telecom sector.
 
• It targets the creation of **Intellectual Property Rights (IPR)** within India to achieve the goals of **Atmanirbhar Bharat**.
 
 
 
• **6G Technology Characteristics:**
 
 
• While **5G** focuses on enhanced mobile broadband, **6G** is expected to offer speeds up to **1 Tbps**, which is nearly **100 times faster** than current 5G peaks.
 
• It will integrate **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** at the physical layer and utilize **Terahertz (THz)** frequencies for massive data transmission.
 
• Key applications include **holographic teleportation**, **Internet of Senses**, and fully autonomous **UAV** (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) networks.

questions.question: By which act did the British government introduce provincial autonomy in India instead of diarchy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935** was a landmark legislation that introduced **Provincial Autonomy**, granting provinces a separate legal identity and autonomy in their executive and legislative spheres.
 
• This Act abolished the system of **Diarchy** (dual government) in the provinces, which had been previously established under the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• The abolition of **Diarchy** meant that the distinction between **Transferred** and **Reserved** subjects at the provincial level was removed, making the provincial executive responsible to the **Provincial Legislature**.
 
• It provided for the appointment of a **Governor** who was advised by ministers, and these ministers were collectively responsible to the elected provincial assembly.
 
• While it ended **Diarchy** in provinces, the Act proposed the introduction of **Diarchy at the Center**, though the federal portion of the Act was never fully operationalized.
 
• The Act also laid the foundation for an **All-India Federation** consisting of British Indian provinces and **Princely States**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act 1919**:

 
 
• Also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, it introduced **Diarchy** in provinces.
 
• It established a **Bicameral Legislature** at the central level for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1909**:
 
 
• Known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, it is infamous for introducing **Separate Electorates** for Muslims.
 
• It increased the size of legislative councils and allowed members to discuss the **Budget** and ask supplementary questions.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1892**:
 
 
• This act expanded the number of non-official members in the councils and introduced a limited form of **indirect elections**.
 
• It empowered the legislative councils to discuss the **Annual Financial Statement** and address questions to the executive.

questions.question: Which battle fought in 1757 marked the beginning of British political control in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** took place on **23 June 1757** in **Palashi**, Bengal, on the banks of the **Bhagirathi River**.
 
• The conflict was fought between the **British East India Company**, led by **Robert Clive**, and the **Nawab of Bengal**, **Siraj-ud-Daulah**.
 
• The British victory was facilitated by the defection of **Mir Jafar**, the Nawab's commander-in-chief, who had entered into a secret treaty with the British to become the next Nawab.
 
• This battle is historically significant as it transformed a commercial entity into a **ruling political power** by providing the British with the vast revenues and resources of **Bengal**.
 
• It laid the foundation for nearly **two centuries** of British colonial rule in the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Buxar (1764)**:

 
 
• Fought between the **British East India Company** and a combined alliance of **Mir Qasim**, **Shuja-ud-Daula** (Nawab of Awadh), and **Shah Alam II** (Mughal Emperor).
 
• It resulted in the **Treaty of Allahabad** in **1765**, which granted the British **Diwani rights** (the right to collect taxes) over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Seringapatam (1799)**:
 
 
• This was the concluding battle of the **Fourth Anglo-Mysore War**.
 
• It resulted in the death of **Tipu Sultan** and the complete **British annexation** of the Mysore territories.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Colachel (1741)**:
 
 
• Fought between the **Kingdom of Travancore** under **Marthanda Varma** and the **Dutch East India Company**.
 
• It is celebrated for being the first time an **Indian kingdom** defeated a major **European naval power**.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Defence, what was India's all-time high defense production in 2024–25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1.54 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Defence** recorded a historic milestone as India's value of defence production reached an all-time high of **₹1.54 lakh crore** in the financial year **2024-25**, reflecting the success of domestic manufacturing policies.
 
• This achievement signifies a robust growth trajectory, driven by the government's strategic focus on the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) initiative to reduce dependence on expensive military imports.
 
• The total production value includes contributions from **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)**, other specialized **Public Sector Undertakings**, and the rapidly growing **Private Sector** industries.
 
• The private sector has seen a significant surge in its contribution, now accounting for a substantial portion of the total production value, supported by the streamlining of **Industrial Licenses** and the ease of doing business.
 
• Strategic policy reforms, including the **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020** and the notification of five **Positive Indigenisation Lists** (covering over 500 items), have been instrumental in reaching this fiscal milestone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defence Exports and Global Reach**:

 
 
• Parallel to the increase in production, India's defence exports have also hit record levels, reaching approximately **₹21,083 crore**, a growth of over **30%** compared to the previous year.
 
• The country now exports advanced military hardware, such as the **BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles**, **LCA Tejas**, and **Advanced Light Helicopters (ALH)**, to more than **85 nations**.
 
 
 
• **Modernization and Innovation**:
 
 
• **iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence)**: This flagship scheme provides a platform for **Startups** and **MSMEs** to co-create high-end technology solutions for the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• **Budgetary Support**: The government has consistently allocated nearly **75%** of the **Defence Capital Procurement Budget** for domestic procurement to sustain this production momentum.
 
• **SRIJAN Portal**: An online indigenisation portal that helps the domestic industry take up the manufacturing of items that were previously imported by **DPSUs**.

questions.question: According to the Henley Passport Index 2025, what is India's rank in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**85**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Henley Passport Index 2025** is a global ranking that categorizes countries according to the travel freedom enjoyed by their citizens, specifically focusing on the number of destinations accessible without a prior visa.
 
• According to the latest report for **2025**, **India** has been ranked at the **85th** position globally.
 
• Holding an Indian passport currently allows citizens **visa-free** or **visa-on-arrival** access to **58** destinations worldwide, including popular spots like **Thailand**, **Mauritius**, and **Indonesia**.
 
• The index serves as a significant indicator of a nation's **geopolitical standing**, diplomatic health, and the strength of its **international reciprocity** agreements.
 
• The rankings are calculated based on proprietary data which reflects the ongoing shifts in **global mobility** and international travel policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henley Passport Index Methodology**:

 
 
• The index is derived from exclusive data provided by the **International Air Transport Association (IATA)**, which maintains the world's most comprehensive travel information database.
 
• It includes **199 different passports** and **227 different travel destinations**, updated in real-time throughout the year as visa policy changes come into effect.
 
 
 
• **Global Top Performers**:
 
 
• **Singapore** consistently maintains its lead as the world's most powerful passport, granting its holders visa-free access to a record **195** destinations.
 
• Other top-tier nations include **France**, **Germany**, **Italy**, **Japan**, and **Spain**, which share high-ranking positions due to extensive European and global diplomatic ties.
 
 
 
• **Lowest Ranked Passports**:
 
 
• **Afghanistan** remains at the bottom of the list (ranked **103rd** or similar depending on the specific update cycle), with access to only **26** destinations, reflecting regional instability and limited diplomatic reach.

questions.question: As part of trade liberalization, in which year did India completely remove Quantitative Restrictions (QRs) on imports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2001**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quantitative Restrictions (QRs)** are non-tariff barriers, such as **quotas** and **import licensing**, used by a government to limit the physical quantity of goods that can be imported over a specific period.
 
• India maintained these restrictions for decades to protect domestic industries and manage **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crises, citing the provisions under the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**.
 
• Following the **Economic Reforms of 1991**, India began a systematic process of **Trade Liberalization** to integrate its economy with the global market.
 
• A significant turning point occurred when the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** ruled against India in a dispute triggered by the **United States**, stating that India’s improved BoP position no longer justified the maintenance of QRs.
 
• Consequently, India committed to a phased removal of these barriers. The final batch of **715 items**, which included **agricultural products** and **consumer goods**, saw the total elimination of QRs on **April 1, 2001**.
 
• This move marked the transition from a **command-based licensing regime** to a **market-linked tariff system**, significantly impacting the **Exim Policy (Export-Import Policy)** of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **New Economic Policy (1991)**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **LPG Model** (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization), it was spearheaded by then Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• It aimed to reduce the **License-Permit Raj**, encourage **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, and dismantle **trade barriers** to boost industrial efficiency.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**:
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 1995**, following the **Uruguay Round** of negotiations, it serves as the global body regulating international trade.
 
• India is a **founding member** and is obligated to adhere to its principles of **most-favored-nation (MFN)** treatment and the reduction of protectionist measures.
 
 
 
• **Tariffication**:
 
 
• After removing QRs, India shifted to **Tariffs** (customs duties) as the primary tool for regulating imports, which is considered a more transparent and less distortionary method of **trade protection**.
